ctx.x: Well, I think that it's interesting that Duke Ellington has developed the reputation that he has. Really, it's an indictment of the criteria of the American public that he is accepted as being a great musical genius. One thing is, of course, that so far as I am able to determine on the basis of what I would consider to be reasonable investigation, first, that he was not, in fact, a composer, that he never really composed anything at all of any significance, certainly none of the things with which his name is…
Jimmy Noon's solo became the Creole Love Call. Yes. Jimmy Noon's solo in one of the King Oliver pieces.

items.q: I am providing this as prime source information because this is the thing that I remember... discussing it with early jazzmen... that they will corroborate this.

ctx.x: Among the, well, of course, uh, it was obvious why anybody would be a King. First, he would have to be able to play a trumpet. As you notice, all of the Kings in the hierarchy are trumpet players. Right. Now, the King must, of necessity, be able to play loud. Mm-hmm. And, a loud lead, since most of the music was played in the street, was an absolute essential, because otherwise, he wouldn't be heard. And most especially, when, when bands were playing in competition with each other, the ones that could play loud…

items.title: Al Rose Interview, 1976-02-19
items.q: The interviewee discusses King Oliver's band and anecdotes about Oliver's playing style in New Orleans/Chicago, but does not claim personal interaction, collaboration, or mentorship with Joe Oliver himself.

ctx.x: Is the, uh, the King Oliver Creole Band of 1923 that played in Chicago, is, does that fit the, uh, description, uh, of a jazz ensemble band?

I would say that it, that it frequently fits the description, but not, not all the time. Uh, by the time you had Oliver in New Orleans, in Chicago, uh, you already had a set band for one thing, which had the opportunity to play a location job for a long period of time. Mm-hmm. And to, uh, to some extent to work out, uh, not exactly arrangements, but to work out, uh, uh, common activities, musically, on the stand. And, uh, of course, you also had, uh, a certain increase in the amount of solo play, which, of…
